questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few cards are bonds. Some bonds are lockers. All lockers are branches.
Conclusions:
I. All cards are branches.
II. No bonds is a branches.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: No cards is a bonds. Some bonds are lockers. All lockers are branches.
Conclusions:
I. All cards are branches.
II. Some branches are bonds.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few cards are bonds. All bonds are lockers. No lockers is a branches.
Conclusions:
I. Some cards are not bonds.
II. No bonds is a branches.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some cards are bonds. All bonds are lockers. No lockers is a branches.
Conclusions:
I. Some cards are lockers.
II. Some bonds are branches.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: U < W > V < S > T.
Conclusions: I. W > T   II. V > T.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
Statements: W = P < X < S = U.
Conclusions: I. S ≥ X   II. U < X.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is definitely true; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
Statements: P < V = W = S = X.
Conclusions: I. S < V   II. X ≤ V.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is definitely true. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
Statements: Q < X = V > S = W.
Conclusions: I. X ≤ S   II. W > Q.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
credit savings banking = ni to ze
credit access digital = re lu to
savings access rural = ka lu ze
banking digital rural = ka ni re
credit savings rural = ka ze to
What is the code for “savings”?
questions.explanation: Answer: ze. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: credit = to, savings = ze, banking = ni, access = lu, digital = re, rural = ka.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 38 km east, turns left and walks 40 km, then turns left and walks 8 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 50. Net displacement is 30 km east and 40 km north. By Pythagoras, √(30² + 40²) = 50 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 17 km east, turns left and walks 20 km, then turns left and walks 2 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?

questions.stem: E is the mother of D. A is the son of D. B is the father of D. How is A related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. B is a parent of D, and A is D’s son. Hence A is B’s grandchild.

questions.stem: A is the brother of E. E is the mother of F. D is the father of A and E. How is A related to F?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. A is the brother of F’s mother E. Therefore A is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: F is the only daughter of D. D is the father of F. C is the son of F. E is the sister of D. How is D related to C?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. D is the father of F, and F is C’s mother. Thus D is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 42 candidates, a candidate is 10th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 30. New front rank = 10+3 = 13. Back rank = 42 − 13 + 1 = 30.

questions.stem: In a queue of 55 candidates, a candidate is 22th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 30. New front rank = 22+4 = 26. Back rank = 55 − 26 + 1 = 30.

questions.stem: An item costs ₹850. It is marked above cost and sold at a 10% discount on marked price, earning 12% profit. Find the marked price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 1057.78. Selling price = 850 × 112/100. Marked price = selling price ÷ 0.9 = 1057.78.

questions.stem: A can finish a job in 16 days and B in 24 days. They work together for 4 days, then B leaves. How many more days does A need? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 9.33. Use 48 work units. Rates: A = 3, B = 2 units/day. Remaining = 48 − 4×5. Divide by A’s rate 3.

questions.stem: A boat travels 105 km downstream and the same distance upstream. Its still-water speed is 11 km/h and stream speed is 4 km/h. Find the total time (hours).
A invests ₹34000 for 12 months. B invests ₹102000 for 9 months. Total profit is ₹136500. Find B’s share (₹).
questions.explanation: Answer: 94500. Capital-time ratio = 12 : 27. B’s share = total × 27/(39) = 94500.

questions.stem: What is the difference (₹) between compound interest and simple interest on ₹17000 at 5% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 42.5. For 2 years, CI − SI = P(r/100)² = 17000 × (5/100)².

questions.stem: A vessel contains 70 litres of milk and water in ratio 3:2. How many litres of pure milk must be added to make the ratio 2:1?
questions.explanation: Answer: 14. Milk = 3V/5, water = 2V/5. Solve (3V/5 + x)/(2V/5) = 2; x = V/5 = 14.

questions.stem: The average of 20 numbers is 42. One number, 54, is replaced and the average rises by 7. What is the new number?
questions.explanation: Answer: 194. Total increases by 20 × 7. New number = 54 + 140.

questions.stem: A father is three times as old as his daughter. After 7 years, their combined age will be 78 years. Find the father’s present age.
questions.explanation: Answer: 48. Let daughter’s age be x. Father is 3x. 4x + 14 = 78; x = 16, so father = 48.
